summary.title: Ten Rules for Negotiating a Job Offer
summary.one_liner: Learn a ten-rule framework for negotiating a job offer, from treating employment as a market deal to keeping options open, protecting salary information, and using competing offers.
keywords: ask for more time to decide offer
takeaways: Treat a job offer as a deal in the labor market, not a favor, and always negotiate.
Get every detail in writing and send confirmation emails to create a paper trail.
Protect information: do not reveal your current pay or reveal your bottom line, and avoid early decision points.
Use other offers and proactive follow-ups to build urgency, since companies value multiple strong signals.
Treat exploding offers (24-72 hour deadlines) as non-offers unless the window is widened, and ask for more time.
summary.summary: This essay by Haseeb Qureshi, a former App Academy instructor and tech job-seeker, lays out ten rules for negotiating a job offer, presented as the first of two parts. It argues that employment is a market deal where you are selling labor, and it walks through the process from receiving an offer to responding to a recruiter's "what do you think?" question. The author uses a watermelon-farmer analogy and sample scripts for staying positive, deferring decisions, and emailing other companies about competing offers. It also explains why companies respond to competing offers, since they are weak signals of quality that combine into a stronger one, and it addresses exploding offers with an example reply.
